headline: Short-term spending law keeps the federal government funded into early March 2024 and extends several expiring health and other programs.
what_it_does: This law is a stopgap funding measure that prevented a government shutdown. It funds agencies covering agriculture, energy and water, military construction and veterans affairs, and transportation and housing through March 1, 2024, and most other agencies through March 8, 2024, generally at 2023 levels. It also extends many expiring programs, including community health center funding, special diabetes programs, child welfare grants, and drone-threat powers, mostly through March 8, 2024. It delays planned cuts to Medicaid payments for hospitals serving many low-income patients and trims two Medicare and Medicaid improvement funds.

who_it_affects.how: Their agencies stay funded, avoiding a shutdown, through March 1 or March 8, 2024.
Federal funding for these clinics serving underserved areas continues through March 8, 2024.

who_it_affects.group: Health care workers in the National Health Service Corps and primary care residents at teaching health centers
who_it_affects.how: Scholarships, loan repayment, and training funding continue through March 8, 2024.

who_it_affects.group: People with Type 1 diabetes and Native American tribal communities
who_it_affects.how: Funding for Type 1 diabetes research and diabetes care programs for tribes continues through March 8, 2024.

who_it_affects.group: Hospitals that treat many low-income Medicaid patients
who_it_affects.how: Scheduled cuts to their extra Medicaid payments are delayed until March 9, 2024.
A minimum adjustment that affects Medicare payment rates in some areas continues through March 8, 2024.

who_it_affects.group: Families and children in the child welfare system
who_it_affects.how: Grants to states and tribes for keeping families together and supporting adoption or reunification continue through March 8, 2024.

who_it_affects.group: Teens and young people in sex education programs
who_it_affects.how: Funding for abstinence-focused and pregnancy-prevention education programs continues through March 8, 2024.

who_it_affects.group: Residents of Micronesia and the Marshall Islands
who_it_affects.how: U.S. grants and financial aid to these nations continue through March 8, 2024.

when_it_takes_effect: January 19, 2024; most funding and extensions last through March 1 or March 8, 2024.
